SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Insect sting to right arm a few minutes ago with localized rash; patient feels mild breathing difficulty and worries about possible swelling of lips/tongue.
- History of present illness:
  • Sting occurred “a few minutes ago.”  
  • Patient uncertain if bee or wasp.  
  • Rash and small puncture mark at sting site; slight soreness, no significant swelling.  
  • Reports mild, non-progressive sensation of breathing difficulty; no current acute distress.  
  • Feels anxious about potential deterioration.
- Past medical history: Eczema; episodic anxiety/panic (never medicated).
- Medications: None; has not yet taken antihistamine.
- Social history: Works as computer scientist; lives alone; owns a cat; nonsmoker/alcohol/drug use not documented.
- Allergies: Penicillin (reaction details not documented).

Objective:
- General: Appears well on video; speaking in full sentences without distress.
- Airway/ENT: Lips and oral mucosa appear normal; no visible swelling; throat clear; no stridor.
- Skin (right arm): Small erythematous area with puncture mark; blotchy rash; no obvious swelling or heat.
- Respiratory: Breathing unlabored on video; no audible wheeze or stridor.
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Investigations: None performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Localized reaction to insect sting
   - Assessment: Localized allergic reaction to likely wasp/bee sting; no evidence of systemic anaphylaxis at present.
   - Differential diagnosis: Early evolving systemic reaction (anaphylaxis) vs localized cellulitis (if rash spreads/warms).
   - Treatment planned:
     • Begin oral antihistamine: Chlorphenamine 4 mg orally, up to 6 times/day, or a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • Educate on red-flag symptoms (lip/tongue swelling, stridor, worsening breathing, rapid rash spread); seek immediate emergency care (A&E) if they occur.  
     • Advise to monitor sting site; if redness spreads, becomes hot, or signs of infection appear, contact clinic; antibiotics may be required.  
     • Provide patient information link on anaphylaxis.
   - Follow-up: Return or call urgently if symptoms worsen; routine follow-up not required if resolves.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected data: No vitals, medication reconciliation, smoking/alcohol status, immunization status, detailed penicillin reaction.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational overlap but clinically intelligible.
